title: A Salt for the Oath
premise: Rafael Ravensworth, a scribe indentured to the Guild of Impossible Things, discovers the guild's ledgers record debts paid in souls—and that her own grandmother sold one generations ago to the court beneath the mountain. When a feral child arrives speaking the pre-kingdom tongue of the deep court, Rafael realizes the girl is the collateral on an oath about to come due: her own bloodline's payment. To save the child and free her family's name, Rafael must steal back the soul from the mountain court, betraying both her guild masters and the man she loves who serves them. She succeeds at terrible cost—paying with her own voice, traded for the child's freedom—and returns to rebuild the guild as something honest, its ledgers finally balanced.
about_author: Silas Crane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing debt records in coastal port cities before turning to fiction. Their work is known for ledger-precise prose and stories where every bargain, magical or mundane, comes due.

chapters.title: The Weight of Ink
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. A day in the life of the Guild of Impossible Things: Rafael copies contracts for bottled storms and borrowed years, her indenture ticking down in the margins. The emotional beat is weary competence masking quiet desperation—she counts the days left on her debt like a prisoner scratches walls.

chapters.title: A Knock Before Dawn
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. A mud-caked child appears at the guild door during a storm, speaking a language no living scholar knows—yet Rafael understands fragments, as if remembering rather than learning. The beat is uncanny dread; the guild master's eyes go hungry when he hears it.

chapters.title: What the Ledgers Owe
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Digging through sealed archives, Rafael finds her grandmother's name beside the word 'collateral' and a debt marked 'due at first moonrise.' The beat is vertigo—the past reaching up through paper to claim her.

chapters.title: The Man Who Counts for the Court
chapters.summary: POV Tomas, guild enforcer and Rafael's secret love. He reports the child's arrival to his true employers below the mountain, torn between duty and the woman he's been ordered to watch. Beat: divided loyalty, tenderness sharpened into betrayal-in-waiting.

chapters.title: First Moonrise
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. The deadline passes unmarked—or so it seems—until the child begins to fade like breath off glass, her edges going translucent each night. Beat: horror dawning slowly; time was never on their side.

chapters.title: Terms of Service
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. The guild master offers Rafael a deal: steal back the soul from the deep court and her indenture is void—but if she fails, the guild keeps the child and Rafael both. Beat: gilded cage closing; she signs because refusing means watching the girl dissolve.

chapters.title: Salt and Small Mercies
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Preparations: salt wards, a stolen key, and the child—who Rafael names Wren—teaching her scraps of the old tongue between nightmares. Beat: fragile found-family warmth before the descent, making what follows hurt more.

chapters.title: The Road Below
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Ordered to intercept Rafael, Tomas instead covers her tracks, lying to the court's heralds for the first time in his career. Beat: the point of no return—he chooses her over everything he was built to be.

chapters.title: Doors That Remember Names
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. At the mountain's root, doors open only for those they recognize; Rafael speaks her grandmother's name and the stone shudders awake. Beat: inheritance as both key and curse—the family debt literally unlocks her path.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. The deep court receives her with courtesy that curdles: lords of old stone who trade in souls the way merchants trade grain, and who already know why she's come. Beat: predatory politeness; every compliment is a hook.

chapters.title: An Audience of Ancestors
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. In the court's vaults Rafael finds her grandmother—not dead but held, her soul serving as the court's living seal. Beat: grief and fury braided together; the theft she planned becomes a rescue she can't abandon.

chapters.title: The Price of Looking Back
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Captured by the court after his betrayal surfaces, Tomas bargains with his own memories as currency to buy Rafael time. Beat: sacrifice without witness—he pays pieces of himself she'll never know about.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Deep
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Studying the court's master ledger, Rafael finds the flaw she needs: every soul-debt has a clause of exchange, but none has ever been invoked against the court itself. Beat: cold clarity—the rules cut both ways if she dares wield them.

chapters.title: Wren Speaks
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The child, fading fast, reveals she remembers being the soul once sold—a grown life compressed into small bones. Beat: devastating innocence; the collateral has been conscious all along.

chapters.title: The Counter-Offer
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael invokes the exchange clause before the assembled court, offering something of equal weight for Wren's soul. The lords laugh—until she names the one thing beneath the mountain that cannot be replaced. Beat: audacity trembling on ruin.

chapters.title: What Cannot Be Replaced
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Her offer: her voice, the instrument of every contract she's ever written and every word she'd ever say to those she loves. The court considers. Beat: the theme made flesh—survival always costs the thing you least can spare.

chapters.title: Sealed in Salt
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Escaping his cell mid-negotiation, Tomas reaches the vault as the bargain closes, arriving in time to hear Rafael give her answer and powerless to stop it. Beat: heartbreak as helplessness; love present but unable to intervene.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Voiceless, Rafael completes the ritual: Wren's soul unwinds from the court's seal, her grandmother crumbles gratefully to dust, and the mountain begins to shake as its anchor fails. Beat: triumph and terror fused—the escape must happen now.

chapters.title: Running Out of Mountain
chapters.summary: POV alternating Rafael/Tomas. The collapsing court chases them through doors that no longer remember names; Tomas carries the weakening Wren while Rafael, mute, leads by memory and gesture. Beat: desperate momentum, trust as the only currency left.

chapters.title: Daylight Debts
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. They surface—but the guild master waits with wardens, claiming Wren per the failed-contract clause. Rafael produces the counter-offer's signed terms: the debt is paid, the child free, and the guild master bound by his own paper. Beat: quiet victory through the very weapon used against her.

chapters.title: A New Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Months later: Rafael, indenture void, takes over the failing guild and begins rewriting its contracts honestly, Wren learning words again beside her, Tomas choosing to stay without being asked. Beat: healing without erasure—scars acknowledged, not hidden.

chapters.title: The First Word
chapters.summary: POV Wren. One year on, Wren writes her first sentence in the old tongue and reads it aloud to Rafael: a promise that what was given will be remembered. Rafael answers with her hands, signing the old language perfectly. Beat: grace note ending—inheritance transformed from debt into gift.
